source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 3 (Metals and Non-metals).

sections.heading: 1. Physical Properties
points: **Metals** — lustrous, malleable, ductile, good conductors of heat/electricity, sonorous, high melting point, solid at room temp (except **mercury**, a liquid).
**Non-metals** — dull, brittle, poor conductors (except **graphite**), not sonorous; may be solid, liquid (bromine) or gas.
Exceptions: **sodium/potassium** are soft (cut with knife); **mercury** liquid; **iodine** lustrous non-metal; **carbon (diamond)** is hardest and highest melting.

sections.heading: 2. Chemical Properties and Reactivity Series
points: Metals react with **oxygen → metal oxides (basic)**; some oxides are **amphoteric** (Al₂O₃, ZnO — react with both acids and bases).
Metals react with **water** (K, Na very vigorously → hydroxide + H₂; less reactive slowly or not at all).
Metals react with **acids → salt + hydrogen** (Cu, Ag, Au do not).
**Reactivity series** (decreasing): **K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > (H) > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au**.
A more reactive metal **displaces** a less reactive one from its salt solution.

sections.heading: 3. Ionic Compounds and Metallurgy
points: **Ionic (electrovalent) compounds** form when metals transfer electrons to non-metals (e.g. NaCl); high melting points, conduct in molten/aqueous state, soluble in water.
**Minerals/ores** — metals occur in earth's crust; extraction = **metallurgy**.

sub: Low reactivity (Au, Ag) — found free / simple heating.
Medium (Fe, Zn, Pb) — roasting/calcination then **reduction** (with carbon/coke).
High (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al) — extracted by **electrolysis** of molten ore.

points: **Thermit reaction** — Al reduces Fe₂O₃ (used to weld railway tracks); Al is a strong reducing agent.

sections.heading: 4. Refining, Corrosion, Alloys
points: **Refining** — impure metal purified by **electrolytic refining** (e.g. copper).
**Corrosion** — reactive metals corrode (iron rusts); prevention: galvanising, painting, oiling, alloying.

**Alloys** — homogeneous mixtures of metals (or metal + non-metal): **steel** (Fe+C), **stainless steel** (Fe+Cr+Ni), **brass** (Cu+Zn), **bronze** (Cu+Sn), **solder** (Pb+Sn); **amalgam** = alloy with mercury.
Alloys have better properties (harder, resist corrosion, lower conductivity/melting point).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Only liquid metal = mercury; non-metal that conducts = graphite; hardest = diamond.
Reactivity series: K>Na>Ca>Mg>Al>Zn>Fe>Pb>H>Cu>Hg>Ag>Au.
Amphoteric oxides = Al₂O₃, ZnO (react with acids and bases).
High-reactivity metals extracted by electrolysis; medium by reduction with carbon.
Brass = Cu+Zn; bronze = Cu+Sn; steel = Fe+C; thermit = Al + Fe₂O₃.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Mercury** is the only metal liquid at room temperature; **graphite** conducts electricity.
**Al₂O₃ and ZnO are amphoteric** (react with both acids and bases).
**Highly reactive metals (Na, K, Ca, Al)** are extracted by **electrolysis**.
**Brass = copper + zinc**; **bronze = copper + tin** (do not swap).
